description:
DataMCP turns your PostgreSQL into an MCP endpoint that Cursor, Claude Desktop, VS Code, and Windsurf can actually use — without handing out raw connection strings to every developer on the team.

**How it works:** connect your database once, set which tables each API key can touch, share the MCP URL. AI tools get schema context and query access. You get an audit trail of every query that ran.

**6 MCP tools:** `query`, `get_schema`, `get_table_details`, `get_permissions`, `get_schema_changes`, `resync_schema`

- Per-table permission controls (read, write, or none — per key)
- AES-256-GCM encrypted credentials
- Full query audit log in the dashboard
- OAuth 2.0 for seamless client authorization
- Free tier available

No self-hosting. No config files on developer machines. Just a URL and an API key.

tools.name: setup
tools.description: Get started with DataMCP. Returns instructions for connecting your first PostgreSQL database.

tools.name: list_connections
tools.description: List all database and API connections for the authenticated user

tools.name: get_schema
tools.description: Get the current database schema for a specific connection

tools.name: search_tables
tools.description: Search for tables by name across all connections

tools.name: list_api_endpoints
tools.description: List all API endpoints for a specific OpenAPI connection

tools.name: search_endpoints
tools.description: Search for API endpoints across all OpenAPI connections

tools.name: get_repository_structure
tools.description: Get the file tree structure of a Git repository

tools.name: get_file_content
tools.description: Get the content of a specific file from a Git repository

tools.name: search_repository_files
tools.description: Search for files in a Git repository by path or extension

tools.name: get_commit_history
tools.description: Get the commit history of a Git repository

limit.description: Maximum number of commits to return (default: 10)

tools.name: get_readme
tools.description: Get the README content of a Git repository

prompts.name: analyze_schema
prompts.description: Review the database schema and surface design issues, missing indexes, denormalization opportunities, and naming inconsistencies.

prompts.name: describe_schema
prompts.description: Generate concise, human-readable descriptions for every table and column that lacks one, using code/migration context.

prompts.name: investigate_issue
prompts.description: Run a structured investigation on a data or behavior issue using SELECTs against this database.

arguments.name: issue
arguments.description: Describe the issue or question (e.g. "users signing up in the last 24h are not getting welcome emails").

prompts.name: find_slow_candidates
prompts.description: Identify tables and query patterns most likely to become performance hotspots, based on the schema alone.
